newsitem.title: USA: Alex Brown says exiting municipal finance sector.
newsitem.headline: Alex Brown says exiting municipal finance sector.

text.p: Alex Brown Inc, the retail brokerage that last month agreed to merge with Bankers Trust New York Corp, said Monday it plans to reorganize its fixed-income operations, reducing its role in that sector.

Chairman A.B. Krongard, in a prepared statement, attributed the downsizing, which includes exiting the fixed-rate municipal finance business and will affect about 160 employees, to how hard it had become to make a profit.

"Even as many other firms left this business, we reorganized and reduced certain operations, grew other areas and offered some new products. However, despite the best efforts of our employees, declining spreads have put pressure on fixed income profitablity, and we have decided not to continue our present role in fixed income," he said.

The firm, which said the transition would begin immediately, added, "It will continue to market variable rate products and aggressively engage in the convertible debt business." Neither Alex. Brown nor Bankers Trust officials were immediately available to elaborate.

The Baltimore-based brokerage, which said it has 2,700 employees, added that it planned to reassign many of the 160 workers who will be affected by the changes, but noted it was not yet clear how many eventually would lose their jobs.
Alex Brown, which expects to complete its merger with Bankers Trust in the fourth quarter, was established in 1800.
